scenes.teacher_script: Today, we'll learn about proper and improper fractions using a delicious analogy: pizza slices!
A fraction represents a part of a whole. Imagine a whole pizza cut into equal slices.
A proper fraction is when the numerator is smaller than the denominator. This means you have less than one whole pizza.

template_data.image_prompt: High-quality realistic photograph of a pepperoni pizza cut into exactly 8 equal slices. 3 slices are slightly pulled away from the main pizza, showing the fraction 3/8. Clean white background, 16:9 ratio, vibrant colors.

scenes.teacher_script: An improper fraction is when the numerator is equal to or larger than the denominator. This means you have one whole pizza or more!

template_data.image_prompt: High-quality realistic photograph of two pepperoni pizzas. The first pizza is whole and cut into 8 equal slices. The second pizza has 3 slices remaining from its original 8 slices. The total number of slices shown is 11 (8+3). Clean white background, 16:9 ratio, vibrant colors.

scenes.teacher_script: Let's compare proper and improper fractions. Remember, proper fractions are parts of a whole, while improper fractions are one whole or more.

bullets: Example: 11/8 (11 slices, where 8 make a whole)

scenes.teacher_script: Improper fractions can also be written as mixed numbers, combining a whole number and a proper fraction. For example, 11/8 is the same as 1 whole pizza and 3 extra slices, or 1 and 3/8.
